exchanges.question: AI cash tool focus for launch, deposit pressure risk, deposit competition with similar smart tools, higher deposit betas?
exchanges.answer: Early stages for product. Look segment by segment how people manage money. High net worth people astute, tons of choices. Question is making easier for them manage money way comfortable. Like enabling checking to money market fund move. Provide great values, have ATMs, branches, advice, Zelle. Look whole basket do better job for client. May squeeze margin, create competition. Not live yet, targeted small client subset with investments where opportunity take larger investment wallet share.

exchanges.question: Basel III capital proposal RWA inflationary impacts. Mitigating actions? Double counting of markets or operational risk relief magnitude?
exchanges.answer: Well-practiced understanding rules, using financial resources efficiently support client franchise. Hope rules land where nothing makes good healthy business completely non-economic. Targeted RWA clarifications needed on high-yield repo collateral and advised lines proposal unclear impact, creates irrational results. Not optimization story; rule set converging, need grow business deploy resources serve clients. G-SIB significant disincentive particular markets business. U.S. capital markets key competitive advantage; regulatory rules discouraging dynamic secondary market with bank participation not great. If double count removed by stress testing removal, no impact; if modifying operational risk RWA calculation, might have impact. Removal definitely support, not number one priority.

exchanges.question: Modified Markets NII outlook due to rate changes. Retain $95B ex-Markets NII? Offsets to higher rates and asset sensitivity if no cuts rest of year?
exchanges.answer: Asset sensitive; rates higher, removal cuts back half. Might expect NII ex-Markets revision up. EAR $1.8 billion. Cuts pretty backdated; impact full year average only about 20 basis points. Upward revision quite small doing that math. Other bits up and down noise, rounding effects. Numbers aren't changed. Not too much to read into it.

exchanges.question: Private credit default cycle, higher defaults, higher severity. What is ultimate loss back to banks? Will it be systemic?
exchanges.answer: No, quite clear. Private credit leveraged lending $1.7 trillion, high yield $1.7 trillion, bank syndicated $1.7 trillion, investment grade debt $13 trillion, mortgage $13 trillion. Weakening in underwriting not just private credit. Credit cycle will happen. Losses worse than expect relative scenario. Don't think systemic at that size. Recessions stress and strain system. Banks most things on top large losses before hit or stressed. What filter through whole system bigger issue. Corporations not too high debt, consumers not too high, excess government debt. Industry surprises people. 2000 utilities telecom, 2008 media newspapers. Something always happens people don't expect.

exchanges.question: Capital management going forward. Still have big buffer above required levels? Updated thoughts capital allocation?
exchanges.answer: Lots excess capital, measure around $40 billion, can change depending ultimate rules. Prefer deploy capital serving clients. More bankers innovation economy, more global banking, commercial banking overseas, opening countries, payment systems, branches, building client base. Not overnight. Goal not deploy capital; build wonderful businesses use capital intelligently developing with client focus. World so big, complex, capital needs. Biggest small business bankers, capital needs countries, remilitarization, infrastructure. Huge capital needs companies, huge mergers. Some companies not big enough serve. More opportunity serve large clients ways need over time. M&A, countries, helping build infrastructure need. Happen over time, not in rush. Preferred using capital not buying back stock today, doing fair value, but buy cheap get ongoing shareholder benefit.

exchanges.question: Long duration capital needs. Private markets balance sheet or big public banks finance? Higher for longer rates impact direct lending BB B refinancing?
exchanges.answer: Banks won't warehouse very long-dated stuff balance sheet. Investment grade or large non-investment grade, private and public markets come together. Make markets, research. Harder for private credit large investment grade though done it. Compete with us, willing too. Take customer side by side bank syndicated loan. Lot creative capital, creative financing. Institutions need long-dated assets, pension plans, Social Security plans. Intermediate, come ideas, put balance sheet. Balance sheet shorter dated. Infrastructure requirements going up dramatically, utilities roads bridges data centers GPUs. All infrastructure today. Serve clients great job. In categories private and public markets come closer, values trading secondary markets. Higher for longer, stagflation, credit spreads gap out, stress and strain leveraged companies refinancing. Fixed. Capital or credit reduction CapEx plans. Not immediate disaster overnight, more stress and strain. Credit cycle worse than people think. Systemic risk. Recessionary behavior.

exchanges.question: Size private credit exposure?
exchanges.answer: Private market exposure means lot different things. NBFI from $330 call report to $160 core, inside $160 about $50 called private credit, portion involving leverage loan investors. Back leverage BDC lending, underwriting diversification cash flow trapping. Core private credit about $60 billion. Other pieces direct lending subscription lines variously in or out different measures.

exchanges.question: Investment banking activity March held up, pushing out pause on activity, pipeline resilience?
exchanges.answer: Activity held up well. Robust result quarter accelerated timing M&A closure, faster than expected regulatory approval. All to good, unrelated overall sentiment. Pipeline resilient, maybe surprisingly given everything. Middle East timelines quite short, deadlines negotiations, reasonable proceed plans hope quick resolutions. Things getting derailed, surprised not see impact sentiment deal decision-making. Right now quite resilient.

exchanges.question: Balance sheet growth markets 20% year-over-year. G-SIB surcharge impact ability grow? Capital decision markets business?
exchanges.answer: Yes, big part reason spent time talking problems surcharge. Disproportionately accrues Markets business, relatively low-risk density stuff client base needs wants. Important regulators think carefully what trying achieve. Use brainpower find ways serve clients properly reduce G-SIB charge, usually called arbitrage. Not sure outcome great for system, will find ways.

exchanges.question: Private credit selection capability. How ensure staying with good guys avoiding bad guys?
exchanges.answer: Quite disciplined on credit. Certain things turn down. Don't like covenants, underwriting, ability move assets secured company. Willing balance sheet go down. Think credit stretched, won't make loans, not because don't want, just not willing meet terms. That's how do it. Most clients including private credit, underwrite company, loans, covenants. Credit's discipline. Loans outcome doing good business. Sometimes loan book drops 10% next year, completely fine thought loans walking away irresponsible.
